name: Learn basic water rescue
blurb: How to help someone in trouble without becoming the second casualty. The whole principle is that you almost never swim to them.
gear: Ideally a lifesaving or beach-safety course
A throw bag or anything buoyant
steps: Learn the order: shout and signal, reach, throw, wade, row — and only swim as an absolute last resort with training.
Reach with anything long: a branch, a paddle, a towel, while lying down and anchored so you cannot be pulled in.
Throw anything buoyant — a ring, a cool box, a football, an empty bottle. It buys them time and calms them.
Learn to recognise real drowning: silent, upright, head back, arms pressing down. It looks nothing like the shouting and waving people expect.
Learn to call for help properly and to send a specific person to do it.
Take a lifesaving course if you spend real time around water, and refresh CPR alongside it.
tips: Drowning people climb their rescuers. Untrained swimming rescues are how would-be rescuers die.
Cold water shock incapacitates in under a minute regardless of swimming ability.
proof: You can explain and demonstrate reach and throw rescues and recognise the real signs of drowning.
